- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in next period; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% in following 2–3 periods.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to hold too high; apply downward bias adjustment of 2–4% for next 3 periods.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; if sentiment shifts sharply from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast by 3–5% immediately.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or negative values, model underperforms; add 1–2% upward bias to forecast to counteract underestimation.
